headline: Visayas Grid Under Red Alert as Available Supply Falls Below Peak Demand
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Under Red Alert as Supply Falls Short | FMB News
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under a Red Alert on August 28 as available capacity stood at 2,307 MW against projected peak demand of 2,402 MW.
deck: NGCP reported 2,307 MW of available capacity against 2,402 MW projected peak demand, with multiple plants unavailable or operating below rated capacity.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines placed the Visayas grid under a Red Alert from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM on Friday, August 28, after available generation fell below projected evening demand.
NGCP put available capacity at 2,307 megawatts against projected peak demand of 2,402 MW. Yellow Alerts were also scheduled from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM and from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM.

sections.heading: Why supply was tight
paragraphs: NGCP said several coal-fired generating units remained unavailable, while other plants were operating at reduced output. The total unavailable or derated capacity was about 979.6 MW.
Limited electricity imports from Mindanao also added pressure to the Visayas grid during the high-demand period.

sections.heading: What the alerts mean
paragraphs: A Yellow Alert is issued when operating reserves are insufficient to meet contingency requirements. A Red Alert is raised when supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid's regulating requirement.

A Red Alert does not automatically mean all customers will lose power, but it signals a heightened risk of rotational outages or other grid-management measures if supply cannot be balanced with demand.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Visayas grid has faced repeated Red and Yellow Alerts in August because of sustained generating-unit outages, deratings and limited reserve margins.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated tight-supply periods raise reliability concerns for households, hospitals, businesses and industrial users and underscore the importance of dependable generation, reserves and transmission support.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Consumers should monitor NGCP and distribution-utility advisories for succeeding alert schedules, plant returns to service and any rotational-interruption notices.
